facts.content: Patient presents with acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea.
facts.source_text: CC: Acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea

facts.content: Symptoms of acute gastroenteritis began approximately three days ago between Monday and Tuesday.
The patient reports profuse, watery, non-bloody diarrhea occurring about hourly.
The patient reports crampy, intermittent pain in the central and lower abdomen.
facts.source_text: Abdominal pain: crampy, central/lower abdomen; intermittent

facts.content: The patient reports nausea and vomiting, especially with milk intake.
The patient feels hot and febrile but has not measured their temperature.
facts.source_text: Feverish sensation: feels hot/febrile, no measured temp

facts.content: The patient is drinking fluids but the diarrhea is ongoing.
facts.source_text: Hydration: drinking fluids but diarrhea ongoing

facts.content: The patient was able to eat lunch today but stools remain loose.
facts.source_text: Appetite: had lunch today but stools remain loose

facts.content: The patient reports that urine is not clearly abnormal and is described as variable.
facts.source_text: Urine: not clearly abnormal; described as variable

facts.content: The patient reports no blood in the stool.
The patient notes that his brother has similar symptoms and no clear dietary trigger has been identified.
facts.source_text: Triggers: brother with similar symptoms; no clear dietary trigger

facts.content: Patient is generally healthy.
Patient has no history of prior surgeries.
Patient uses paracetamol as needed.
Patient is advised to start or continue oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte over the counter.
Paracetamol as needed is recommended for fever or pain.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient's father has colon cancer currently in the third stage.
facts.source_text: FHx: Father with colon cancer (currently in third stage)

facts.content: The patient smokes socially.
The patient drinks alcohol occasionally.
The patient works in a government office in central London.
facts.source_text: works in a government office in central London;

facts.content: The patient lives with his mother and sister.
The patient's brother has also been ill recently.
Acute gastroenteritis with diarrhea predominance and crampy abdominal pain is diagnosed with a risk of dehydration.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis, diarrhea-predominant, crampy abdominal pain; dehydration risk

facts.content: Family history is notable for colon cancer in the father, currently advanced.
facts.source_text: 2) Family history notable for colon cancer (father, currently advanced)

facts.content: The patient is advised to start or continue oral rehydration solution such as Dioralyte obtained over the counter.
The patient is advised to maintain clear fluid intake and follow a soft diet such as soup and mashed foods, advancing as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Maintain fluids (clear fluids); soft diet (soup, mashed foods) and advance as tolerated

facts.content: Paracetamol as needed is recommended for fever and pain control.
The patient is advised to avoid alcohol.
No antibiotics are prescribed at this time and supportive care is to be continued.
facts.source_text: No antibiotics prescribed at this time; continue supportive care as outlined

facts.content: If symptoms are not improving within 48 hours the patient should contact or return for reassessment.
facts.source_text: If symptoms not improving within 48 hours, contact/return for reassessment
